standard_prerequisites.name: Kleene T-predicate
standard_prerequisites.statement: T(e,x,s) is a primitive recursive relation holding when s codes a halting computation of machine e on input x; phi_e(x) converges iff some s satisfies T(e,x,s).
standard_prerequisites.use: Both halves rest on it: enumerability is witnessed by T-predicate search, and the minimal-s construction h(x) makes the characteristic function computable.

core_obligations: Statement (lines 678-682): A is computable iff both A and its complement are computably enumerable.
Forward half (proof lines 684-688): A computable gives the complement computable (characteristic function composed with 1-minus), hence both c.e.

Converse half (lines 690-703): A = dom(phi_d) and complement A = dom(phi_e); define h(x) = mu s (T(d,x,s) or T(e,x,s)), total by hypothesis; then x in A iff T(e,x,h(x)), a computable relation, so A is computable.
proof_roadmap: Handle the easy direction by complementing the characteristic function.
Write both c.e. sets as domains via phi_d and phi_e.
Define h by minimal search over the disjoined T-predicates and decide membership by T(e,x,h(x)).
difficulty_reason: Characterisation theorem (statement 678-682, proof 684-703): both directions fully carried, the converse hinges on one minimal-search construction. H2.
